newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU gives go-ahead for Palestinian trade deal.
newsitem.headline: EU gives go-ahead for Palestinian trade deal.

text.p: The European Union pledged on Tuesday to continue financial support for the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and approved plans to include the fledgling Palestinian entity in a lucrative Mediterrannean trade bloc.

EU foreign ministers approved a proposal by the European Commission for Palestinian authorities to be included in the so-called Euromed accord, which governs the 15-nation bloc's relations with Mediterranean partners.

The timing of the mandate will be seen as a boost for Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat as he prepares for a U.S.-led peace summit in Washington later on Tuesday with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

The summit was called by U.S. President Bill Clinton to try to salvage a Middle East peace process threatened by a week of fighting sparked by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel under Temple Mount in Jerusalem -- a site holy to both Jews and Moslems.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel welcomed the EU's commitment to financial support, saying: "We have concentrated our efforts more on the economic side and it should remain that way."
Some EU states -- notably France -- have been angered at being left out of the Washington summit, but Kinkel said the EU should not be "overambitious".
"It does not mean Europe should be absent in the political realm," Kinkel said." But we have to accept the more important role of the United States."

The Euromed Accord -- which aims to turn the Mediterranean region into a free-trade zone -- offers lucrative financial incentives to non-EU countries in order to bring their economies into line with the 15-nation bloc.
The mandate given to the commission to negotiate Palestinian entry means the fledgling territory could be included by the end of this year.

The EU is the biggest donor of financial aid to Palestinian authorities and since 1993 has contributed over 320 million ecu European currency units ($400 million) to development of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
This assistance will continue until 1998 with the EU committed to at least 50 million ecu a year in further development grants.
A statement by the Commission -- the EU's executive -- said the agreement would comply with all World Trade Organisation rules.
It said the agreement would allow Palestinian authorities to group all goods produced for export in the West Bank or Gaza Strip under one point of origin label -- important for EU import regulations.

While the agreement seeks trade reciprocity, it does allow for some protection by the Palestinians of industries considered "fragile". This would allow them to restrict certain EU imports or impose tariffs on them.
Approval for the mandate comes after a rash of diplomatic activity between the EU and Palestinian authorities ahead of the Washington summit.

Arafat met some EU foreign ministers in Luxembourg on Monday night on his way to Washington where he asked for more financial assistance to offset the effects of the border closure with Israel. He said this was costing Palestinians some $6 million to $7 million a day.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said the border closure meant EU aid intended for reconstruction was having to be diverted to prop up the economy. ($1=.8010 Ecu)
